samuel2.21.p1.b1.text: During the reign of David there was a famine for three successive years, and David sought the face of the LORD.

samuel2.21.p1.b2.text: “It is because of the blood shed by Saul and his family, because he killed the Gibeonites.”

samuel2.21.p1.b3.text: The Israelites had taken an oath concerning them, but in his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul had sought to kill them.

samuel2.21.p1.b4.text: “What shall I do for you? How can I make amends so that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD?”

samuel2.21.p2.b1.text: “As for the man who consumed us and plotted against us to exterminate us from existing within any border of Israel, let seven of his male descendants be delivered to us so that we may hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.”

samuel2.21.p2.b3.text: Now the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD between David and Jonathan son of Saul.

samuel2.21.p2.b4.text: … they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

samuel2.21.p3.b1.text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. … she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day,

samuel2.21.p3.b2.text: nor the beasts of the field by night.

samuel2.21.p3.b3.text: From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, …

samuel2.21.p3.b4.text: When David was told what Saul’s concubine Rizpah, daughter of Aiah, had done,

samuel2.21.p4.b1.text: He went and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, …

samuel2.21.p4.b2.text: … along with the bones of those who had been hanged.

samuel2.21.p4.b3.text: And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in Zela in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul’s father Kish. After they had done everything the king had commanded,

samuel2.21.p4.b4.text: God answered their prayers for the land.

samuel2.21.p5.b1.text: Once again the Philistines waged war against Israel, and David and his servants went down and fought against the Philistines;

samuel2.21.p5.b3.text: Then Ishbi-benob, a descendant of Rapha, whose bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels and who was bearing a new sword, resolved to kill David.

samuel2.21.p5.b4.text: “You must never again go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished.”

samuel2.21.p6.b1.text: Some time later at Gob, there was another battle with the Philistines. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, one of the descendants of Rapha.

samuel2.21.p6.b2.text: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

samuel2.21.p6.b3.text: And there was still another battle at Gath, where there was a man of great stature with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all.

samuel2.21.p6.b4.text: And when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of David’s brother Shimei killed him.

samuel2.21.p6.b5.text: So these four descendants of Rapha in Gath fell at the hands of David and his servants.
